title: Derecognition is permanent and cross-role: losing one AC role bars you from the other
content:
A.1.5.10 defines derecognition as "the ultimate accountability measure for misalignment," entailing "permanently removing the individual or entity from their role as an Alignment Conserver," and adds the cross-role bar: "An individual/entity who has been derecognized from a Facilitator role is not eligible to serve as an Aligned Delegate, and vice versa."

The cross-role clause closes an obvious loophole. Without it, derecognition would function as a lateral move — a removed facilitator could reappear as a delegate, retaining influence over governance while shedding the finding. Since both roles are Alignment Conserver roles held to the same general requirements (A.1.5.6), a finding of misalignment in one is equally disqualifying in the other; the roles differ in function, not in the alignment they demand.

It also interacts with the single-role rule (A.1.5.5) to make the AC track a genuinely all-or-nothing commitment: one role at a time, and one strike removes access to all of them.

What gives the provision teeth in practice is publication. A.1.5.10.1 requires derecognition notices to be "issued publicly," with justification and reasoning provided — and A.1.5.10.2 records each one as Active Data listing "the identity and known aliases or associated entities," maintained by the Core Facilitator under the 'Alignment Conserver Changes' protocol. The bar is enforced by a public register rather than by a technical control, which is the only option available for a role that is pseudonymous by design.
description: A.1.5.10 makes a derecognized Facilitator ineligible to serve as an Aligned Delegate and vice versa, so the sanction removes an actor from the AC track rather than from one seat.
